what_it_proves: The statutory notes quantify gross derivative assets used in the legal entity.
boundary: Gross derivative assets are not hedge cost

what_it_proves: The statutory notes quantify the nonadmitted portion of derivative assets.
boundary: Nonadmitted classification does not identify economic hedge effectiveness or cash cost.
next_proof: Reconcile admitted/nonadmitted treatment to statutory surplus and hedge economics.

what_it_proves: The statutory notes quantify admitted derivative assets.
boundary: Admitted derivative assets are not available owner cash and may hedge policyholder guarantees or asset risks.
next_proof: Join admitted derivatives to Schedule DB positions and investment-income effects.

what_it_proves: The statutory notes report aggregate deferred interest associated with the investment-income disclosure.
boundary: Deferred interest is not automatically a derivative premium or liability cost.
next_proof: Reconcile deferred interest to the relevant asset and derivative schedules.

what_it_proves: The statutory notes report cumulative PIK interest included in current principal balances.
boundary: PIK is an accrual/valuation component and not collected cash or owner cash.
next_proof: Identify the affected assets and separate accrued from collected income.

what_it_proves: The notes identify options futures variance swaps swaptions and interest-rate swaps used to hedge indexed-annuity crediting and asset-liability rate mismatches.
boundary: No quantified hedge expense settlement or product-level attribution is disclosed in these pages.
next_proof: Obtain Schedule DB and derivative cash-flow/gain-loss detail with product or liability allocation.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB Part A reports the prior-year book/adjusted carrying value for options caps floors collars swaps and forwards.
boundary: This is a derivative opening balance rather than owner cash or a policyholder-cost allocation.
next_proof: Reconcile Part A rows to Schedule DB verification and product/liability hedge assignment.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB Part A reports consideration received or paid on terminated derivative contracts during the year.
boundary: The amount is a statutory derivative termination-flow control and is not automatically net cash available to policyholders

what_it_proves: Schedule DB Part A reports total gain or loss on derivative termination recognized during the year.
boundary: This is not a complete hedge return and does not establish cash settlement net of premiums
column12: Join terminated-contract rows to realized gains/losses

what_it_proves: Schedule DB Part A reports current-year unrealized valuation changes across open and terminated derivative sections.
boundary: Unrealized valuation is not collected cash or distributable earnings.
next_proof: Separate open-position marks from settled cash and reconcile to investment income and surplus.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB Part A reports amortization affecting derivative book/adjusted carrying value.
boundary: Amortization is an accounting movement and not a standalone hedge cash cost or owner-cash deduction.
next_proof: Map amortization to contract type and statutory income recognition.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB Part A reports foreign-exchange changes affecting derivative carrying value.
boundary: FX movement is not a realized cash loss or liability-cost allocation by itself.
next_proof: Separate settled FX cash from valuation movement and identify hedged assets/liabilities.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB Part A reports the ending book/adjusted carrying value for options caps floors collars swaps and forwards.
boundary: The page-level value has a one-dollar difference versus the later verification control and is not owner cash.
next_proof: Use the Schedule DB verification page as the controlling reconciliation.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB Part B reports cumulative cash change for futures contracts.
boundary: This is futures-level cash movement and not a complete derivative portfolio cash flow or policyholder funding cost.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB Part B reports ending statement value for futures contracts.
boundary: It does not identify hedge effectiveness or cash available after liability claims.
next_proof: Reconcile futures rows and variation margin to the derivative verification.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB book/adjusted carrying value verification closes within one dollar.
next_proof: not a return or cash-availability conclusion.
column11: Preserve the one-dollar source tolerance while joining underlying rows.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB fair-value verification closes within one dollar.
boundary: Fair value is not collected cash or owner cash.

what_it_proves: Schedule DB potential-exposure verification closes exactly at the displayed control.
boundary: Potential exposure is a risk measure
next_proof: not a realized liability or cash payment.
